order_note: No predecessor. SQL 169 replaces one foreign key and creates nothing (owner 2026-11-16, two checks could not be deleted, the API refusing "This check cannot be deleted because it has dependent financial/provider records (check_billing_events)"; asked what a delete of a check with a charge should do, the owner chose "Delete, keep charge (Recommended)"). check_billing_events_check_intake_item_id_fkey, FOREIGN KEY (check_intake_item_id) REFERENCES public.check_intake_items(id) ON DELETE CASCADE (the Supabase inline key, supabase/migrations/20260501204336), becomes the same key ON DELETE SET NULL under the same name, so deleting a check keeps its check_billing_events rows with check_intake_item_id NULL and every other column unchanged; the billing engine reads charges with LEFT JOIN check_intake_items, so an unlinked charge still counts. Accepted predecessor exactly the CASCADE key; the file refuses (55000) sql169_prerequisite_missing, sql169_column_not_nullable (the column NOT NULL: Supabase dropped it in 20260605163443) and sql169_unexpected_foreign_key (no key on check_intake_item_id, more than one, another name or another definition), and leaves an already SET NULL key as it is (sql169_foreign_key_already_current). No CHECK constraint requires the column; the unique indexes on it treat NULL as distinct or are partial on IS NOT NULL; SQL 154's starter-package trigger fires on UPDATE OF status only. The applying login must own check_billing_events (altered_relations_owned_by_login). No function, trigger, policy, grant, column or row changes. Expected pre-state in both environments: the CASCADE key, validated (release sql169 v1: f7530ea5e4b9ff3d8dc74911ffeadfe9b38dd6fd867ca3edacbc9ec65c8c4a40, releaseStateHash('sql169', that key)). The API keeps refusing such a delete until its own later change (a Lambda overlay of the delete-check code, after this pin is applied in production). No API, Lambda or SPA change is part of this pin.
